The primitives form a triadic structure: Git OIDs define temporal state, hash integrity ensures data consistency, and POSIX modes govern access control. These interact as a closed-loop system where each element validates the others—OIDs provide sequence, hashes validate content, and permissions enforce policy. Failure in one component disrupts the entire chain. For example, an altered hash without corresponding OID change suggests tampering, while a missing permission implies unauthorized access. The system's robustness relies on mutual verification across these dimensions.
